Subject: Re: Capacity planning — request to formalize MAP and lead-time assumptions

Hi Mina / Ben,

Thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, Helix needs a short, executable Mutual Action Plan that captures:
- Dedicated vs Private lead-time assumptions (procurement, provisioning, network peering)
- GPU pool sizing options for 3 ramp scenarios (Pilot, Ramp, Steady)
- Acceptance criteria / staged cutover checklist (SOC2 gating + perf SLAs)
- Contracting milestones and procurement packet for our Legal/Procurement teams

Can you drop a draft MAP and an initial sizing recommendation by EOD tomorrow? Procurement would also like a one-page summary they can attach to the PO.

Rajeev
VP, Infrastructure
Helix Labs

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — request to formalize MAP and lead-time assumptions

Thanks Rajeev — we can do that. High-level proposal below; attached is a one-page MAP and a sizing summary (Helix_MAP_v1.xlsx) for your procurement packet.

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Target region: us-west-2 for pilot to minimize latency to your prod region.
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated pool for pilot (predictable throughput), with optional Private VPC cutover in Ramp stage.
- Lead times: 10–12 weeks for Dedicated reserved pool (hardware allocation + infra staging), 14–18 weeks for Private (network + KMS + on-prem approvals).
- GPU type baseline: 8 x A100-80GB equiv nodes for Pilot, scale to 32 nodes for Ramp, 48 nodes Steady (mix of q8/float depending on quality gating).
- Buffer / waterfall: we recommend a 20% burst buffer for the first 6 weeks post-cutover; reduces to 10% after stabilization.

MAP milestones (draft):
1) Eval window (2 weeks): sample workloads + perf targets; Redwood provides eval cluster + test harness.
2) Procurement & PO (2–4 weeks concurrent with eval): finalize terms, sign PO for initial tranche.
3) Hardware allocation (8–12 weeks from PO for Dedicated; 12–18 for Private).
4) Staging & QA (2 weeks): SOC2 evidence snapshot, perf SLOs verified on pilot traffic.
5) Phased cutover (3 waves across 4 weeks): canary -> partial -> full.

Acceptance criteria (short list):
- 95th percentile token latency within agreed threshold on pilot test corpus.
- No regressions in quality (prompt set A/B) beyond 2% for critical prompts.
- Audit logs and KMS integration validated for Private deployments.

Deliverables attached: Helix_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + milestone dates), gpu_pool_spec_sheet.pdf (hardware profile). We can iterate once procurement confirms the PO cadence.

Next steps: if this looks OK, Ben / Karthik will prepare the PO packet and we’ll lock milestone dates.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Helix_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx), gpu_pool_spec_sheet.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rajeev Malhotra <rajeev@helixlabs.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixlabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — request to formalize MAP and lead-time assumptions

Rajeev — quick operational notes to help Procurement:

- We can split the initial commitment into a Pilot tranche (3 months) + Ramp tranche (6–12 months) to shorten lead time to first usable capacity. PO language should allow staged tranches and a billing credit for early termination within the Pilot period.
- DocuSign: I’ve attached a PO template and a sample SOW outline. Procurement will want explicit acceptance gates tied to the MAP stage dates.
- Risk: if Helix requires Private on-prem earlier than 12 weeks, there will likely be a 3–5 week network/KMS window we cannot compress without air-gapped logistics — call this out in the PO.

Suggested immediate asks for your procurement team:
1) Approve Pilot tranche (A100-80GB x8 equivalent) — triggers hardware staging.
2) Confirm billing contact and invoicing cadence.
3) Set primary acceptance metric: 95th pct latency <= 250ms on sample corpus.

I’ll drop the PO template into the DocuSign link and share the HubSpot deal for tracking.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redwood_PO_Template_v3.docx (docx), MAP_SOW_outline.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Capacity planning — request to formalize MAP and lead-time assumptions

Thanks — this is very helpful. Procurement is OK to approve the Pilot tranche and will circulate a PO by EOD Fri. A couple of clarifications before we sign:
- Can Redwood commit to an internal escalation SLA for any provisioning delays (we may need to trigger alternate region fallback)?
- For the acceptance test, can you share the exact test harness and dataset so our QA can validate locally prior to staging?

Once Procurement sends the PO we’ll mark the deal as HLX-2457 and route it to Finance. Please add the DocuSign link to the HubSpot record.

Rajeev
